traits.habitat_notes: Coastal dunes, bluffs and terraces, estuary margins (FNA, introduced in California and Florida from South Africa); planted on road banks.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form chosen from the plant's habit: a carpet of trailing succulent stems with crossing pairs of three-angled finger-like leaves and large yellow many-petalled flowers.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species.

allometry.note: 0.3 m tall at 6 years in the open, inside the floras' range of heights, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Every look comes from the characters through the library's rules: a carpet of trailing succulent stems with crossing pairs of three-angled finger-like leaves and large yellow many-petalled flowers.

traits.library_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): succulent subshrubs: the library's succulent class.

traits.life_span.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): succulent subshrubs.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stems to 3 m; bark persistent, leathery: woody at the base only, read as semi.

traits.leaf_habit.note: English Wikipedia, Carpobrotus edulis (read 2026-10-19): grows year round; the leaves persist (succulent groundcover).

traits.stem_posture.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stems trailing, mat-forming, rooting at nodes.

traits.clonal.note: English Wikipedia, Carpobrotus edulis (read 2026-10-19): stoloniferous growth and clonal integration; FNA stems root at the nodes.

traits.stem_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stems to 3 m (genus 5-30 dm); Wikipedia: shoots grow more than 1 m a year.

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: a mat of prostrate stems with ascending leaves and flowering shoots, about 10-30 cm deep; no flora gives a height.

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: mats piled on themselves or scrambling over shrubs to about 0.5 m.

traits.crown_width_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: one plant's stems run to 3 m in each direction (FNA), so about 6 m across before rooting stems make a clone.

traits.clone_radius_m.note: English Wikipedia, Carpobrotus edulis (read 2026-10-19): it can grow to at least 50 m in diameter.

traits.bark_texture.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): bark persistent, leathery; no fissures described, read as smooth.

traits.rosette.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves cauline, in pairs along the trailing stems.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves opposite, slightly connate basally.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): opposite pairs; decussate assumed as for the family's opposite-leaved mesembs.

traits.leaf_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade thick, fleshy, sharply 3-angled in cross-section (no vocabulary state for a trigonous blade; it is a blade, not a needle).

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade 5-11 x 1-1.5 cm, widest below the middle, sharply 3-angled with a concave upper side: in outline long and narrow, read as linear.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade 5-11 cm.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade 1-1.5 cm wide.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves sessile.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): outer angle serrate near the apex (Wikipedia: serrated sides near the tips).

traits.leaf_apex.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the 3-angled blade tapers to a pointed tip; acute.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): glabrous.

traits.leaf_posture.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves curve up from the prostrate stems (Wikipedia: very slightly curved).

traits.leaf_colour.note: English Wikipedia, Carpobrotus edulis (read 2026-10-19): leaves dull green or yellow-green, fading to pink with age; FNA leaves green; sRGB by eye for 'dull green'.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers solitary.

traits.pedicel_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pedicel 20-60 mm.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers 8-10 cm across; Wikipedia 6.4-15.2 cm, taken as low and high.

traits.perianth.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (read 2026-10-19): the showy 'petals' are petaloid staminodes, linear, many, in several series; drawn as a perianth of many parts in a spiral, the nearest the flower card draws.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): calyx lobes 4-5 (2 large outer, 2-3 inner); C. edulis lists 2 outer and 3 inner, so 5.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals yellow, aging pink (pink-flowered wild plants are hybrids); sRGB by eye for 'yellow'.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals distinct, spreading in many rows: rotate.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens 100 per series, 4(-7) series: about 400 (to 700); the genus says to 600.

traits.stamen_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens 6-8(-12) mm.

traits.anther_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): anthers yellow; sRGB by eye for the word.

traits.filament_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens yellow; sRGB by eye for the word.

traits.style_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): style absent; stigmas radiating over the fruit, 8-15 mm (the stigma rays stand where a style would).

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pistil 8-12-carpellate (the species is not given separately).

traits.ovary_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): ovary inferior.

traits.hypanthium.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Aizoaceae family account (Vivrette, Bleck & Ferren) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): hypanthium present; Wikipedia: receptacle wedge-shaped, tapering into the pedicel.

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowering year-round, mostly spring (California). A look has one season a year that begins with its buds, so year-round flowering is drawn as February to December, buds showing in late January (a library gap: no season yet runs all year).

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (Vivrette) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): berries, fleshy, edible, indehiscent.

traits.fruit_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits clavate to subglobose, depressed at the top.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits 20-35 mm.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits yellowish; Wikipedia ripening from green to yellow; sRGB by eye for 'yellowish'.

traits.fruit_colour_ripening.note: English Wikipedia, Carpobrotus edulis (read 2026-10-19): fruit ripening from green to yellow; sRGB by eye for 'green' (taken as the leaf's green).

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: no source gives the fruiting season; with mostly spring flowers in California, fruits ripen through summer into autumn.

traits.elevation_min_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): 0-100 m.

traits.elevation_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): 0-100 m.

traits.light.note: English Wikipedia, Carpobrotus edulis (read 2026-10-19): flowers open in bright sunlight; a pioneer of open dunes.

traits.moisture.note: English Wikipedia, Carpobrotus (read 2026-10-19): drought tolerant; sandy coastal habitats of Mediterranean climates.

traits.soil_texture.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): coastal dunes, bluffs and terraces (sand, rock).

traits.habitat_notes.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): coastal dunes, bluffs and terraces, margins of estuaries; planted along highways and for dune stabilization.

traits.perianth_parts.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read counts it: FNA: petaloid staminodes many, in 2-4 series, so about a hundred; the card draws at most 60. They are linear, 30-40 mm long (FNA), stated before as petal_length_m and petal_shape, which a spiral perianth does not take.

traits.leaf_succulence.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus (read 2026-10-19): leaves thick and fleshy, rounded-triangular to sharply three-angled in section.

traits.leaf_cross_section.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Carpobrotus edulis (read 2026-10-19): blade sharply three-angled in section, the upper face concave; Wikipedia the same.

traits.shoot_leaves.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read counts it: trailing stems 1-3 m set with crossing pairs of leaves 4-13 cm long, the pairs about 10 cm apart and crowded toward the tips.
